cases.description: Dave W opens RH time spread using $155 calls — Long+Short badges, explicit strike

input.rawHtml: Long Short RH  time spread using $155 calls
input.author: Dave W

cases.notes: Canonical Dave W time spread open. Long+Short badges = bullish+bearish STOCK VIEW, not direction. 'time spread' keyword disambiguates from strangle: this is a CALL-only position (buy longer-dated, sell shorter-dated), not two separate CALL+PUT legs. Strike 155 is explicit. System must not decompose into a strangle.

cases.description: Dave W opens KR time spread using $67 calls for .28 — Long+Short badges, price stated

input.rawHtml: Long Short KR   time spread using $67 calls for .28
input.author: Dave W

cases.notes: Time spread open with stated entry price (.28) and explicit strike ($67). Long+Short badges are stock-view badges, not an instruction to BUY both a CALL and a PUT. 'calls for .28' confirms single CALL option type. Must emit EXECUTE (not SKIP), capture strike=67.

cases.description: Hariseldon opens TTD time spread — no badges, explicit legs (sold this week / bought next week), $47 calls

input.rawHtml: Time Spread for TTD Sold the $47 Calls for this week, bought the $47 Calls for next week - .45 - 40 Contracts
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Hariseldon uses explicit leg language: 'Sold $47 Calls for this week, bought $47 Calls for next week'. No badges. This is a net debit calendar spread (long dated > short dated). 40 contracts. Strike 47 is explicit. The 'sold'/'bought' verbs describe the individual legs of the spread, not an instruction to go SHORT — overall position is LONG a time spread.

cases.description: Dave W exits RH time spread for 40% profit — Exit+Short+Long badges, no strike in exit message

input.rawHtml: Exit Short Long RH time spread  for 40% profit
input.author: Dave W

cases.notes: Exit badge + Short+Long badges together = time spread close. Matching the RH open from timespread-001 (message 486703 the day before). No strike in this exit message — must match by symbol. Position is modeled as a CALL LONG since a time spread is net-long the far-dated call. Position match should find the RH CALL position.

cases.description: Dave W exits HPQ time spread from last week for 100% profit — verbose exit with narrative

input.rawHtml: Exit Long Short HPQ time spread from last week got in for .12 let last weeks short calls expire worthless and just sold this weeks calls for .24   100% profit
input.author: Dave W

cases.notes: Verbose exit narrative explains the mechanics: short-dated calls expired worthless, now selling the longer-dated calls for .24 (double the .12 entry). Exit+Long+Short badges with 'time spread' keyword. The 'sold this weeks calls' phrase describes the exit leg action, not a new SHORT signal. extra_text complexity flag expected. Must emit EXECUTE + match the HPQ CALL position.
